stem:
Omkar studies the four-sided figure drawn below. It is tilted on the page. Every side is $3$ cm, and every corner is $90^\circ$.

What is the figure?

options.text: A rectangle only, because any four-sided shape with right angles is called a rectangle and not a square.
A square, from the equal sides alone, without using the right-angle marks.
A square, because all sides are equal and all angles are $90^\circ$, even though it is rotated.
Not a square, because rotating the shape is what changes its side lengths and angles.

teacher.key_rationale: Equal sides and four right angles make a square. Rotation does not change lengths or angles, so the tilted drawing is still a square.
teacher.figure_note: Rotated square with equal sides and right angles marked.
